C0.quote: identify a strongly supported proposal from a space of alternatives
C0.note: Borderline. A deliberation and coalition-formation process aggregates agents' approvals of proposals into a collective choice of the most-supported proposal, framed as pre-vote deliberation.

C1.quote: the deliberation process is guaranteed to terminate
C1.note: Main results are termination bounds and success guarantees for coalition-formation dynamics (transition systems) in various metric spaces. This analysis of non-strategic dynamics fits none of the listed types well.

C2.1.value: approval set; proposals agents approve/support; deliberative coalition structure
C2.1.quote: the set X v is the approval set of v

C2.2.quote: when x >v r we say that v approves x
C2.2.note: Approvals are derived from agents' locations in a metric space: v approves x iff x is closer to v than the status quo.

C2.3.quote: an agent v is able to articulate whether she (strictly) prefers
C2.3.note: Preferences over the status quo and agent locations (ideal points) in a metric space.

C2.4.quote: agents are not strategic: they truthfully reveal whether they support
C2.4.note: Approval is defined as preferring x to the status quo. The conclusion states truthful revelation; abstracting from strategic issues is stated without justification.

C3.1.quote: in our current model agents are not strategic

C3.2.quote: they truthfully reveal whether they support a given proposal

C3.3.quote: strategic issues that may arise during communication
C3.3.note: The paper says it abstracts away from strategic issues and flags game-theoretic extension as future work; no justification is given.

C4.1.note: No utility, welfare, satisfaction, cost or distortion notions are used for voters; only distances determine approval.

C4.2.note: The term dichotomous preferences is not used.

C5.1.quote: the set of most-supported alternatives is M ∗ = argmaxx∈X\{r} |V x |
C5.1.note: Success is defined by maximum approval support. This is not framed as welfare, efficiency, satisfaction, representation or distortion.

VOT.quote_behav: in our current model agents are not strategic
VOT.note: Agents move between coalitions via permitted transitions. Moves are motivated as 'myopically optimize the size of their coalition', but the paper explicitly says agents are not strategic and analyses all runs.

OTH.note: An external mediator is mentioned informally but not modelled.

C9.2.note: Needed assumptions: approvals reflect preferences over the status quo, agents are non-strategic, and agents follow the specified transitions. All are stated.
